question: I need to know a good quick summary of the Microsoft document or the research whatever it said about how the more context and continuity you give to an agent the better it's gonna help the human, I'm trying to make this case in a meeting next week and I need to be able to pull easily from the relevant statistics or research and whatever Microsoft has got that's like visually interesting and helpful for this
answer:
Short answer
- The report’s core finding: agents that keep and use more context and continuity (memory of past interactions, role- and task-specific context, handoffs over time) deliver bigger benefits to people — but this requires team readiness, oversight, and design to avoid overreliance. (See New-Future-Of-Work-Report-2025.pdf, pp.42, 49, 55.)

Key evidence & numbers you can quote (copyable for a slide or meeting)
- “Benzing et al.’s (2025) survey of 1,800 global full‑time English‑speaking employees found that 2 in 3 employees report trusting AI agents; however, 60% skip accuracy checks in AI output.” — New-Future-Of-Work-Report-2025.pdf, p.55.
- “Teams with strong AI readiness (including skills and literacy) report greater individual and collective value from AI, such as higher productivity, better decision‑making, and more creative, collaborative teams.” — New-Future-Of-Work-Report-2025.pdf, p.55.
- The report presents design examples that depend on continuity: “Instant Recaps,” “Adaptive Handoff,” and “Project Browsers” to support work across time (i.e., memory + handoff features) — New-Future-Of-Work-Report-2025.pdf, Fig. 42.1, p.42.
- It also shows a “Team Agent Readiness” cycle (understanding which tasks suit agents, trust, shared outcomes, skills, openness) — New-Future-Of-Work-Report-2025.pdf, Fig. 55.1, p.55.

Visuals the report provides (recommended to use in your slide)
- Team Agent Readiness cycle (clear, compact visual illustrating the components teams need to realize agent benefits). Use this as your headline visual:
  ![Source figure](fli-image:report-document:1:244)
  Source: New-Future-Of-Work-Report-2025.pdf — Fig. 55.1 (page 55).
- Timeline / continuity UI mockups (shows concrete product features that implement continuity: recaps, adaptive handoff, project browsers) — New-Future-Of-Work-Report-2025.pdf, Fig. 42.1 (page 42).
- Ditto / Context+Recap example (how an agent with prepared context and conversation recaps extends a person’s availability) — New-Future-Of-Work-Report-2025.pdf, Fig. 49.2 (page 49).

One-slide script / talking lines (short, punchy)
- Slide headline: “More context + continuity = more useful agents (but teams must be ready)”
- Bullet 1 (evidence): “Surveyed employees trust agents (2/3), yet 60% skip accuracy checks — so trust alone isn’t enough; continuity must be paired with verification and oversight.” — (New-Future-Of-Work-Report-2025.pdf, p.55).
- Bullet 2 (design point): “Features that preserve context across time — instant recaps, adaptive handoffs, project browsers — let agents act as productive collaborators rather than one‑off tools.” — (Fig. 42.1, p.42).
- Bullet 3 (organizational readiness): “Teams that are skilled, aligned on outcomes, and open to integrating agents report larger gains — invest in readiness (training, norms, governance).” — (Fig. 55.1 & surrounding text, p.55).

Caveats to mention briefly
- The report warns of overreliance and skipped checks: design for verification, explainability, and transparent handoff/oversight (New-Future-Of-Work-Report-2025.pdf, pp.29, 55).
- Many visuals are conceptual (designs and qualitative cycles), not causal proof: they synthesize research and field studies; use the survey numbers (p.55) as the strongest quantitative support.

If you want, I can:
- Produce a one‑slide PowerPoint that places the Fig. 55.1 image on the left and the 3 short bullets + the two quoted stats on the right (I’ll cite the pages on the slide).
- Or draft a 2‑minute speaking script that uses the exact wording and cites the page numbers to read in the meeting.

This report is a product of Microsoft's New Future of Work Initiative

Microsoft has shaped information work for over 50 years and the New Future of Work (NFW) initiative has helped it navigate the past five years of profound transformation. While the initiative was born out of the COVID-19 pandemic and subsequent shifts to remote and hybrid work, since 2023 it has focused on the incorporation and growing role of tools powered by large AI models.

Throughout this transformative period, the NFW initiative has brought together researchers from across Microsoft to conduct primary research and synthesize existing findings from the literature. The goal is not merely to predict what changes are coming, but to actively create a new future of work that is equitable, inclusive, meaningful, and productive.

The fifth edition of the annual NFW report represents another year of research and analysis, adding to the growing body of knowledge on Al and work. The evidence and insights presented here are not monolithic and represent contributing researchers' perspectives rather than Microsoft's corporate views. Additional research papers, practical guides, and white papers are available at: aka.ms/nfw.

Overview

Workstreams Publications Videos News & features

The New Future of Work is a cross-company research initiative dedicated to creating solutions for a future of work that is meaningful, productive, and equitable. It began during the pandemic in response to an urgent need to understand remote work practices. When many people returned to the office, the focus shifted to supporting the hybrid work transition. Then in 2023, another generational shift in work occurred when language models made the leap from the lab into the real world, a shift that could make the changes to remote and hybrid work look small by comparison.

The future of work with Al is not a forgone conclusion, and this initiative exists to not just study work with Al, but to help Microsoft build a new future of work with Al that empowers every person on the planet.

This site features research from the initiative that has been published in peer-reviewed scientific venues, as well as resources to help you navigate a rapidly changing work environment and thrive in the age of Al. We recently published our 2024 Report that summarizes some of the exciting work in this space.

Workplace learning can combat AI overreliance and cognitive atrophy

· Blind trust (Benzing et al., 2025), overreliance (Passi et al., 2024), and cognitive offloading (Gerlich, 2025) are risks of human-Al interactions. Benzing et al.'s (2025) survey of 1,800 global full-time English-speaking employees found that 2 in 3 employees report trusting AI agents; however, 60% skip accuracy checks in AI output.

· Workplace learning plays a crucial role in combatting these risks, while also driving the employee engagement and resilience required for successful AI workforce transformation (Malik & Garg, 2017). Teams with strong Al readiness (including skills and literacy) report greater individual and collective value from Al, such as higher productivity, better decision- making, and more creative, collaborative teams (Benzing et al., 2025; Xue & Song, 2025).

· Human-Al interactions that are discursive and progressive promote cognitive enrichment and combat cognitive atrophy (Danry et al., 2023), which are the core elements of traditional Socratic learning methods used to develop metacognition and critical thinking.

· Given its ability to provide personalized, adaptive, role- and task-based learning while incorporating context, memory, and conversational turns, AI presents a promising new learning modality (Joshi, 2025; Tomitsu, 2025). There is opportunity to develop novel interactive learning experiences, like assessment-based dialogic questioning (Hung et al., 2024), to drive employee engagement through workplace upskilling.
